name: Arma 3
author: ops@refx.example
description: Bohemia's military sandbox. SteamCMD-installed dedicated server with mod and mission support.

installScript.script:
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail
# --- ReFx SteamCMD update safety (injected) --------------------------------
# Guards every Steam update: a stuck/partial SteamCMD run (state 0x6, "Missing
# file permissions", ENOSPC, transient failure) must NOT be reported as success
# — that strands the server on a stale build ("wrong build" on join). We key off
# the app's manifest StateFlags: exactly "4" == fully installed & current.
REFX_APPID="233780"
refx_steam_manifest() { echo "/mnt/server/steamapps/appmanifest_${1}.acf"; }
refx_steam_installed() { local m; m="$(refx_steam_manifest "$1")"; [ -f "$m" ] && grep -Eq '"StateFlags"[[:space:]]+"4"' "$m"; }
refx_steam_heal() { # drop a stale/partial manifest so this update re-acquires cleanly
  local m; m="$(refx_steam_manifest "$1")"
  if [ -f "$m" ] && ! refx_steam_installed "$1"; then
    echo "[refx] steam app $1: a previous install left a stale manifest (not fully-installed) — clearing so this update re-acquires the build cleanly."
    rm -f "$m" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  rm -rf "/mnt/server/steamapps/downloading/$1" "/mnt/server/steamapps/temp/$1" 2>/dev/null || true
}
refx_steam_verify() { # HARD-FAIL if the app is not fully installed after the update
  if refx_steam_installed "$1"; then
    echo "[refx] steam app $1 is on the current build (SteamCMD confirmed fully installed)."
    return 0
  fi
  echo "[refx] ERROR: SteamCMD did not finish updating app $1 — the game files were NOT"
  echo "[refx] changed, so the server is still on its previous build and clients may see a"
  echo "[refx] 'wrong build' / version-mismatch error on join."
  echo "[refx][diag] install uid:gid = $(id -u 2>/dev/null):$(id -g 2>/dev/null)"
  df -h /mnt/server 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/[refx][disk] /' || true
  ls -ln /mnt/server 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/[refx][diag] /' | head -20 || true
  # Clear the stale manifest so the NEXT update self-heals (clean re-acquire).
  rm -f "$(refx_steam_manifest "$1")" 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "[refx] Cleared the stale manifest — run Update again and it will re-download the"
  echo "[refx] current build. Your world/config under the data dir are untouched."
  exit 1
}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
refx_steam_heal "$REFX_APPID"

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server
# Locate or bootstrap steamcmd (the parkervcp/steamcmd image does NOT ship it
# on PATH; eggs are expected to fetch it themselves).
if command -v steamcmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  STEAMCMD=steamcmd
else
  echo "[steam] bootstrapping steamcmd"
  mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
  curl -sSL https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar zxf - -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
  chmod +x /mnt/server/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh /mnt/server/steamcmd/linux32/steamcmd 2>/dev/null || true
  STEAMCMD=/mnt/server/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh
fi
# The HOST game-download account uses a node-level home (REFX_NODE_STEAM_HOME,
# mounted by the agent) so its Steam Guard machine-auth persists across servers
# — a code is only needed once per node. Each account gets its OWN subdir, so
# switching the game-download account never reuses or refreshes a previous
# account's cached Steam session. Falls back to a per-server home on older agents.
SERVER_HOME=/mnt/server/.steamhome
mkdir -p "$SERVER_HOME"
if [ -n "${REFX_NODE_STEAM_HOME:-}" ]; then
  GAME_HOME="$REFX_NODE_STEAM_HOME/${STEAM_GAME_USERNAME:-anonymous}"
else
  GAME_HOME="$SERVER_HOME"
fi
mkdir -p "$GAME_HOME" 2>/dev/null || GAME_HOME="$SERVER_HOME"
# BASE GAME download uses the HOST's game-download account (Admin → Settings →
# Steam). Arma 3's dedicated server (233780) is NOT anonymous.
if [ -n "${STEAM_GAME_USERNAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${STEAM_GAME_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  GLOGIN=(+login "$STEAM_GAME_USERNAME" "$STEAM_GAME_PASSWORD")
  [ -n "${STEAM_GAME_GUARD:-}" ] && GLOGIN+=("$STEAM_GAME_GUARD")
else
  GLOGIN=(+login anonymous)
  echo "[steam] No game-download account configured (Admin → Settings → Steam). Arma 3 requires one that owns the game."
fi
# Build ONE steamcmd session: base game update + every Workshop item, so there's
# a single login (avoids Steam login rate limits). On a mods-only Workshop sync
# (REFX_WORKSHOP_SYNC) the base game validation is skipped when already installed.
WS_APP="${WORKSHOP_APP_ID:-107410}"
SC=(+force_install_dir /mnt/server "${GLOGIN[@]}")
if [ "${REFX_WORKSHOP_SYNC:-0}" = "1" ] && { [ -f /mnt/server/arma3server_x64 ] || [ -f /mnt/server/arma3server ]; }; then
  echo "[steam] mods-only sync — skipping base game validation"
else
  SC+=(+app_update 233780 validate)
fi
if [ -n "${WORKSHOP_ITEMS:-}" ]; then
  for id in $WORKSHOP_ITEMS; do SC+=(+workshop_download_item "$WS_APP" "$id" validate); done
fi
SC+=(+quit)
# stdin from /dev/null so a Steam Guard prompt can't hang the install forever —
# it fails fast instead, and the server is marked crashed with this hint.
# Completion tracking: a content/<id> dir is NOT a safe "complete" signal —
# validate-retries write into it mid-download, so a timed-out item can leave a
# PARTIAL dir behind. Within this run we trust only steamcmd's own
# "Success. Downloaded item <id>" stdout line (teed to WSLOG); dirs that
# existed BEFORE this run started were completed by a previous run and are
# trusted (their retries would be a full re-validate of every mod, every run).
WSLOG="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || echo /tmp/refx-workshop.log)"
: > "$WSLOG"
PREOK=" "
for id in ${WORKSHOP_ITEMS:-}; do
  [ -d "/mnt/server/steamapps/workshop/content/$WS_APP/$id" ] && PREOK="$PREOK$id "
done
HOME="$GAME_HOME" "$STEAMCMD" "${SC[@]}" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee -a "$WSLOG" || echo "[steam] steamcmd exited with an error. Missing Workshop items are retried below (downloads RESUME where they left off). If the LOGIN itself failed and the account uses Steam Guard, set a fresh EMAIL code in Admin -> Settings -> Steam (mobile 30s codes expire during steamcmd's self-update) and reinstall; the node is remembered after the first success."
# Big Workshop mods (multi-GB terrains like CUP) routinely hit steamcmd's fixed
# download timeout ("ERROR! Timeout downloading item ...") and abort the WHOLE
# session, killing every later +workshop_download_item too. Downloads resume
# where they left off, so retry just the still-missing items (bounded). One
# login per ATTEMPT, not per item, to respect Steam login rate limits.
ws_missing() {
  local out=""
  for id in $WORKSHOP_ITEMS; do
    case "$PREOK" in *" $id "*) continue;; esac
    grep -q "Success. Downloaded item $id " "$WSLOG" 2>/dev/null && continue
    out="$out $id"
  done
  printf '%s' "$out"
}
if [ -n "${WORKSHOP_ITEMS:-}" ]; then
  # UNCAPPED retry-until-done: every timed-out attempt BANKS resumable
  # progress (steamcmd resumes mid-file), so the loop keeps going for AS LONG
  # AS BYTES KEEP GROWING - a mod of any size completes in one install run.
  # Termination is the progress guard, not a count: 4 consecutive attempts
  # with zero new bytes means an item is removed/private/inaccessible (those
  # fail instantly, not by timeout) and retrying cannot help. The 200 ceiling
  # is a runaway backstop only (~200 GB of banked progress), never the limiter.
  last_bytes="-1"; stall=0
  for attempt in $(seq 1 200); do
    MISSING="$(ws_missing)"
    [ -z "${MISSING// /}" ] && break
    bytes="$(du -sb /mnt/server/steamapps/workshop 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"; bytes="${bytes:-0}"
    if [ "$bytes" = "$last_bytes" ]; then
      stall=$((stall+1))
      if [ "$stall" -ge 4 ]; then
        echo "[workshop] no download progress across 4 consecutive attempts - stopping retries."
        echo "[workshop] This usually means an item is private/removed/inaccessible rather than slow;"
        echo "[workshop] check the still-missing ids on the Steam Workshop and remove any delisted ones."
        break
      fi
    else
      stall=0
    fi
    last_bytes="$bytes"
    # Rotate the list by attempt so ONE grinding multi-GB item (which times out
    # and aborts the batch tail every session) can't starve the other items:
    # each attempt a different item leads, small items drain out, and the giant
    # keeps resuming at the back until only it remains.
    set -- $MISSING
    n=$(( (attempt - 1) % $# ))
    i=0; while [ $i -lt $n ]; do first=$1; shift; set -- "$@" "$first"; i=$((i+1)); done
    echo "[workshop] resume attempt $attempt (unlimited while downloads progress) for missing item(s): $*"
    RC=(+force_install_dir /mnt/server "${GLOGIN[@]}")
    for id in "$@"; do RC+=(+workshop_download_item "$WS_APP" "$id" validate); done
    RC+=(+quit)
    HOME="$GAME_HOME" "$STEAMCMD" "${RC[@]}" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee -a "$WSLOG" || true
    sleep 5
  done
  MISSING="$(ws_missing)"
  if [ -n "$MISSING" ]; then
    echo "[workshop] ERROR: still missing after the resume attempts:$MISSING"
    echo "[workshop] Very large mods can exceed one install run. Run Update (or Workshop -> Apply) again -"
    echo "[workshop] downloads continue where they left off and complete across runs. Nothing is lost."
  else
    echo "[workshop] all Workshop item(s) downloaded."
  fi
fi
# Post-process Workshop items: lowercase (Linux is case-sensitive), symlink, keys.
if [ -n "${WORKSHOP_ITEMS:-}" ]; then
  for id in $WORKSHOP_ITEMS; do
    src="/mnt/server/steamapps/workshop/content/$WS_APP/$id"
    [ -d "$src" ] || { echo "[workshop] $id not downloaded"; continue; }
    find "$src" -depth | while read -r p; do
      b="$(basename "$p")"; lb="$(printf '%s' "$b" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
      [ "$b" = "$lb" ] || { pd="$(dirname "$p")"; [ -e "$pd/$lb" ] || mv "$p" "$pd/$lb"; }
    done
    ln -sfn "steamapps/workshop/content/$WS_APP/$id" "/mnt/server/@ws_$id"
    mkdir -p /mnt/server/keys
    find "$src" -iname '*.bikey' -exec cp -f {} /mnt/server/keys/ \; 2>/dev/null || true
  done
fi
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/arma3server_x64 ] && [ ! -f /mnt/server/arma3server ]; then
  echo "ERROR: Arma 3 server files are missing — set a game-download Steam account (Admin → Settings → Steam) that owns Arma 3, then reinstall."
  exit 1
fi
# Steam API runtime: Arma 3 (a Steam-API game) SIGSEGVs INSTANTLY on launch with
# NO output if it can't dlopen steamclient.so from ~/.steam/sdk{32,64}. steamcmd
# scatters that file across version-dependent locations (its own linuxXX dirs, or
# the login HOME's .steam/.local), so locate it ROBUSTLY by arch and warn LOUDLY
# if missing — a silent miss here is the classic "exited code 139, no .rpt" crash.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32 /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
sc_find() { # $1 = 32|64 — first steamclient.so whose path names that arch
  find "$GAME_HOME" /mnt/server/steamcmd /mnt/server/.steam /root/.steam /root/.local /usr 2>/dev/null \
    -type f -name steamclient.so \( -path "*linux$1*" -o -path "*sdk$1*" \) -print 2>/dev/null | head -n1
}
SC32="$(sc_find 32)"
SC64="$(sc_find 64)"
# steamclient.so dlopens sibling libs (libtier0_s.so, libvstdlib_s.so) from its
# OWN directory; a lone copy of a freshly self-updated steamclient against
# stale/absent siblings fails SteamAPI init on boot ("SteamAPI initialization
# failed") and every client join then dies with "Steam Authentication Failed".
# Stage the MATCHED family from the same steamcmd build next to every copy.
sc_family() { # $1 = source steamclient.so  $2... = destination dirs
  local srcdir dst; srcdir="$(dirname "$1")"; shift
  for dst in "$@"; do
    mkdir -p "$dst" 2>/dev/null || true
    cp -f "$srcdir/steamclient.so" "$dst/steamclient.so" 2>/dev/null || true
    for lib in libtier0_s.so libvstdlib_s.so crashhandler.so; do
      [ -f "$srcdir/$lib" ] && cp -f "$srcdir/$lib" "$dst/$lib" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
  done
}
if [ -n "$SC32" ]; then sc_family "$SC32" /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32; echo "[refx] steamclient.so (32-bit) + siblings staged from $(dirname "$SC32")"; else echo "[refx] WARN: 32-bit steamclient.so not found at install time"; fi
if [ -n "$SC64" ]; then
  # Arma's 64-bit binary also probes next to itself; stage the family there too.
  sc_family "$SC64" /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64 /mnt/server
  echo "[refx] steamclient.so (64-bit) + siblings staged from $(dirname "$SC64") into ~/.steam/sdk64 and the server root"
else
  echo "[refx] WARN: 64-bit steamclient.so NOT found at install time. The runtime launcher will try to supply it from the game image; if it still segfaults (code 139), reinstall once steamcmd has fully self-updated."
fi
# Steam identity: steamcmd DOWNLOADS the dedicated-server app (233780), but the
# server must IDENTIFY as the game (107410) — client tickets are issued for the
# game appid, and a 233780 identity rejects every join with
# "invalid ticket: Game mismatch - Ticket invalid".
echo 107410 > /mnt/server/steam_appid.txt

# Seed a minimal valid server.cfg / basic.cfg from the panel variables if absent
# (the server boots into the lobby; admins edit these via the file manager).
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/server.cfg ]; then
  cat > /mnt/server/server.cfg <<CFGEOF
hostname = "${SERVER_NAME:-A ReFx Hosting Arma 3 Server}";
password = "${SERVER_PASSWORD:-}";
passwordAdmin = "${SERVER_PASSWORD:-changeme}";
maxPlayers = ${MAX_PLAYERS:-32};
battleyeLicense = 1;
persistent = 1;
voteThreshold = 0.33;
kickDuplicate = 1;
class Missions {};
CFGEOF
fi
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/basic.cfg ]; then
  cat > /mnt/server/basic.cfg <<BCFGEOF
MaxMsgSend = 128;
MaxSizeGuaranteed = 512;
MaxSizeNonguaranteed = 256;
MinBandwidth = 1048576;
MaxBandwidth = 251658240;
MinErrorToSend = 0.001;
MinErrorToSendNear = 0.01;
BCFGEOF
fi

# Write the ReFx launcher that runs the server and streams its RPT log to the
# panel console (Arma logs detail to the .rpt file, not stdout).
cat > /mnt/server/refx-run.sh <<'RUNEOF'
#!/bin/bash
# ReFx launcher for Arma 3: runs the dedicated server AND streams its RPT log to
# stdout, because Arma writes its detailed output to a timestamped .rpt file (in
# the profiles dir) rather than to stdout. This makes the panel console useful.
set -u
cd /home/container 2>/dev/null || cd "$(dirname "$0")"
PROFILES="$PWD/serverprofile"
mkdir -p "$PROFILES"

# ---- Panel settings -> server.cfg, applied on EVERY boot -------------------
# Arma reads server.cfg at startup only; syncing here means "save in the
# Startup tab, restart, it's live" (name/slots show in the in-game browser).
# Only panel-owned keys are touched; the rest of server.cfg stays yours.
CFGF="$PWD/server.cfg"
[ -f "$CFGF" ] || printf 'class Missions {};\n' > "$CFGF"
# Raw-editor saves can leave server.cfg with no trailing newline; a plain append
# then glues the key onto the last line and re-appends a duplicate next boot
# (Arma dies every boot with "Member already defined"). Guarantee the newline,
# and sync strip-then-append so each boot rewrites panel-owned keys
# deterministically and self-heals already-glued/duplicated copies.
[ -s "$CFGF" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c1 "$CFGF")" ] && echo >> "$CFGF"
cfg_esc() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '"[:cntrl:]|&'; }
# Value shapes the panel ever writes: "quoted" (Arma doubles inner quotes),
# {array} — both quote-balanced so a removal can never leave a line with an
# odd number of quotes — or a bare scalar. Anything else sharing the key's
# line is customer text and must survive the strip.
CFGV='("([^"]|"")*"|\{[^}"]*("[^"]*"[^}"]*)*\}|[^;"{}]*)'
# Remove every assignment of a panel-owned key wherever an old launcher or a
# raw edit left it: on a line of its own, ahead of customer text on the same
# line, glued to the end of another statement, spread over a multi-line array,
# or malformed — without touching lookalike text inside quoted values.
cfg_strip() { # $1 = key as an ERE fragment (arrays pass e.g. 'headlessClients\[\]')
  sed -i -E \
    -e "\%^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*$CFGV[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*\$%Id" \
    -e "s%^([[:space:]]*)$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*$CFGV[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*%\1%I" \
    -e "s%;[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*$CFGV[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*\$%;%I" \
    -e "\%^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*\{[^}]*\$%I,\%\}%d" \
    -e "/^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=/Id" \
    "$CFGF"
}
cfg_set() { cfg_strip "$1"; printf '%s = %s;\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$CFGF"; }
cfg_set hostname "\"$(cfg_esc "${SERVER_NAME:-A ReFx Hosting Arma 3 Server}")\""
mp="$(printf '%s' "${MAX_PLAYERS:-32}" | tr -cd '0-9')"; [ -n "$mp" ] && cfg_set maxPlayers "$mp"
if [ -n "${SERVER_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
  cfg_set password "\"$(cfg_esc "$SERVER_PASSWORD")\""
  cfg_set passwordAdmin "\"$(cfg_esc "$SERVER_PASSWORD")\""
fi
# Headless BattlEye license acceptance — without it BE never initialises and
# clients loop on "cannot find channel" until kicked.
cfg_set battleyeLicense 1
# Headless clients (AI offload for Antistasi/Liberation-style missions): the
# allowlist arrays are rewritten every boot — the panel adds/removes 127.0.0.1
# for its own in-container HCs, and any other IPs found in them (added via the
# raw editor for remote/self-hosted HCs) are captured first and preserved.
hc="$(printf '%s' "${HEADLESS_CLIENTS:-0}" | tr -cd '0-9')"; hc="${hc:-0}"
hcextra="$(awk 'tolower($0) ~ /^[[:space:]]*(headlessclients|localclient)\[\][[:space:]]*=/ { grab=1 } grab { print; if (index($0, "}") > 0) grab=0 }' "$CFGF" | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | grep -vFx '"127.0.0.1"' | sort -u | tr '\n' ',')"
hcextra="${hcextra%,}"
cfg_strip 'headlessClients\[\]'
cfg_strip 'localClient\[\]'
hcallow=""
[ "$hc" -gt 0 ] && hcallow='"127.0.0.1"'
[ -n "$hcextra" ] && hcallow="${hcallow:+$hcallow,}$hcextra"
if [ -n "$hcallow" ]; then
  printf 'headlessClients[] = {%s};\nlocalClient[] = {%s};\n' "$hcallow" "$hcallow" >> "$CFGF"
fi
echo "[refx] server.cfg synced (hostname, maxPlayers${SERVER_PASSWORD:+, password}, battleyeLicense${HEADLESS_CLIENTS:+, headlessClients})"

# BattlEye needs a WRITABLE dir of its own to drop/update BEServer_x64.so.
mkdir -p "$PWD/battleye"

# Steam API env: Arma's libsteam_api.so reads these; without them (or without
# steamclient.so reachable) the server SIGSEGVs at init with no output.
# GAME appid (107410), NOT the 233780 download app — see the install-time note:
# a 233780 identity makes client ticket validation fail with "Game mismatch".
export SteamAppId=107410
export STEAMAPPID=107410
export SteamGameId=107410
echo 107410 > "$PWD/steam_appid.txt" 2>/dev/null || true

# Safety net (runs INSIDE the real game image): guarantee steamclient.so exists in
# ~/.steam/sdk{32,64}. If the install step couldn't supply it, pull a copy off the
# runtime image — this is the layer most likely to have a valid one.
ensure_sc() { # $1 = 32|64
  local dst="$HOME/.steam/sdk$1/steamclient.so"
  [ -f "$dst" ] && return 0
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.steam/sdk$1"
  local src
  src="$(find "$HOME" /usr /opt /root /home 2>/dev/null -type f -name steamclient.so \( -path "*linux$1*" -o -path "*sdk$1*" \) -print 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
  [ -n "$src" ] && cp -f "$src" "$dst" 2>/dev/null && echo "[refx] supplied steamclient.so (sdk$1) from $src"
}
ensure_sc 32
ensure_sc 64
if [ ! -f "$HOME/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so" ]; then
  echo "[refx] WARN: no 64-bit steamclient.so available — arma3server_x64 will likely SIGSEGV. Reinstall the server to fetch it."
fi

BIN=./arma3server_x64
[ -x "$BIN" ] || BIN=./arma3server
# Mirror the proven upstream Pterodactyl egg's invocation (bind all, BattlEye path,
# relative profiles). Arma writes its .rpt under the profiles dir.
ARGS=(-ip=0.0.0.0 -port="${SERVER_PORT:-2302}" -config=server.cfg -cfg=basic.cfg -bepath="$PWD/battleye" -profiles="$PROFILES" -name=refx)
# Auto-init (panel Startup-tab toggle): load the mission cycle (class Missions
# in server.cfg) at boot so the persistent mission runs without waiting for an
# admin to log in. Requires persistent = 1 (seeded by default). Harmless when
# class Missions is empty.
case "$(printf '%s' "${AUTO_INIT:-}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in 1|true|yes|on) ARGS+=(-autoInit);; esac
# Build the -mod list: user-specified MODS plus the enabled Workshop items the
# panel downloaded (symlinked as @ws_<id> by the install step).
MODLIST="${MODS:-}"
for id in ${WORKSHOP_ITEMS:-}; do
  d="@ws_$id"
  [ -e "$d" ] || continue
  case ";$MODLIST;" in *";$d;"*) ;; *) MODLIST="${MODLIST:+$MODLIST;}$d";; esac
done
[ -n "$MODLIST" ] && ARGS+=(-mod="$MODLIST")
# Server-side mods (-serverMod): loaded by the SERVER process only - never
# advertised to clients and not loaded by the headless clients below
# (anti-cheat like infiSTAR must not run on an HC).
[ -n "${SERVER_MODS:-}" ] && ARGS+=(-serverMod="$SERVER_MODS")

SRV=
HCPIDS=""
shutdown() {
  [ -n "$SRV" ] && kill -TERM "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  for p in $HCPIDS; do kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null; done
}
trap shutdown TERM INT

# Arma needs to find its bundled libsteam_api.so (server dir) AND steamclient.so
# (~/.steam/sdk64) at runtime.
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PWD:$PWD/.steam/sdk64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
# Container-wide OOM-kill counter (cgroup v2, then v1), read before launch and
# after exit: a raised count is definitive proof the kernel killed for RAM —
# the one crash Arma can never log itself.
oom_count() {
  n="$(awk '/^oom_kill /{print $2}' /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.events 2>/dev/null)"
  [ -n "$n" ] || n="$(awk '/^oom_kill /{print $NF}' /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.oom_control 2>/dev/null)"
  printf '%s' "${n:-0}"
}
OOM0="$(oom_count)"
START_TS=$SECONDS
echo "[refx] launching: $BIN ${ARGS[*]}"
# Capture the server's own stdout/stderr so a startup crash is visible (Arma is
# otherwise silent until the .rpt appears).
"$BIN" "${ARGS[@]}" > "$PWD/arma3-console.log" 2>&1 &
SRV=$!
tail -n +1 -F "$PWD/arma3-console.log" 2>/dev/null &

# Headless clients: same binary, -client -connect to the local server, same mod
# list, own profile dir each. They live inside this container, so they share the
# plan's CPU/RAM limits and their traffic never leaves localhost (no extra ports,
# no BattlEye exposure — the cfg allowlists 127.0.0.1 above). Spawned after a
# grace period so the server is up before they knock; each writes its own log.
if [ "${hc:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  [ "$hc" -gt 3 ] && hc=3
  echo "[refx] starting $hc headless client(s) for AI offload (logs: hc<n>.log; mission must support HCs)"
  n=1
  while [ "$n" -le "$hc" ]; do
    (
      sleep 25
      exec "$BIN" -client -connect=127.0.0.1 -port="${SERVER_PORT:-2302}" \
        ${SERVER_PASSWORD:+-password="$SERVER_PASSWORD"} \
        -profiles="$PWD/hcprofile$n" -name="hc$n" \
        ${MODLIST:+-mod="$MODLIST"} > "$PWD/hc$n.log" 2>&1
    ) &
    HCPIDS="$HCPIDS $!"
    n=$((n+1))
  done
fi

# Follow the newest RPT to stdout, re-targeting when Arma rotates the file.
(
  last=
  while kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; do
    f="$(find "$PROFILES" -type f -name '*.rpt' -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -n1 | cut -d' ' -f2-)"
    if [ -n "$f" ] && [ "$f" != "$last" ]; then
      last="$f"
      echo "[refx] streaming Arma 3 log: ${f##*/}"
      tail -n +1 -F "$f" 2>/dev/null &
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
) &

# Wait for the server to exit, surviving the SIGTERM that triggers graceful stop.
while kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; do wait "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; done
RC=$?
UP=$((SECONDS - START_TS))
echo "[refx] arma3server exited (code $RC) after ${UP}s."
# Say what the code MEANS — a bare number sends customers hunting. The OOM
# counter is checked first: it outranks the code (an OOM kill of a headless
# client can surface as any exit shape of the main process).
OOMK=$(( $(oom_count) - OOM0 ))
if [ "$OOMK" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "[refx] OUT OF MEMORY: the kernel's OOM killer fired ${OOMK} time(s) this run — the server hit the plan's RAM limit."
  echo "[refx] Antistasi-style missions grow as they run, and EACH headless client loads the full mod set."
  echo "[refx] Fix: fewer headless clients, a smaller mod set, or more RAM on the plan."
elif [ "$RC" = 137 ]; then
  echo "[refx] Code 137 = killed (SIGKILL). If you didn't press Kill, this is almost always the RAM limit."
elif [ "$RC" = 139 ] && [ "$UP" -lt 30 ]; then
  echo "[refx] Code 139 = crashed at startup — usually a missing/incompatible steamclient.so; run a Reinstall/Update to refresh it."
elif [ "$RC" = 139 ]; then
  echo "[refx] Code 139 = the game segfaulted mid-run — usually a mod or mission bug rather than the host; check recently updated mods."
fi
echo "[refx] --- last server stdout/stderr ---"
tail -n 80 "$PWD/arma3-console.log" 2>/dev/null
RPT="$(find "$PROFILES" -type f -name '*.rpt' -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -n1 | cut -d' ' -f2-)"
if [ -n "$RPT" ]; then
  echo "[refx] --- last lines of ${RPT##*/} ---"
  tail -n 50 "$RPT" 2>/dev/null
elif [ "$UP" -lt 30 ]; then
  echo "[refx] (no .rpt written — the crash was before Arma init; the output above is the reason.)"
else
  echo "[refx] (no separate .rpt — the Linux server logs to the console output above.)"
fi
RUNEOF
chmod +x /mnt/server/refx-run.sh
refx_steam_verify "$REFX_APPID"
echo 'Arma 3 install complete.'

variables.description: Name shown in the in-game server browser.
Leave blank for a public server.

Extra, manually-uploaded mod folders to load IN ADDITION to your Workshop mods, semicolon-separated (e.g. @my_clan_mod;@private_fix). Upload the folder via SFTP/Files first. Steam Workshop mods do NOT go here - manage those on the Workshop tab.

Server-only mods loaded with -serverMod, semicolon-separated (e.g. @infiSTAR_A3). Loaded by the server process ONLY: never advertised or sent to players, and not loaded by headless clients - the right place for anti-cheat and server-side tools. Upload the mod folder to the server root via SFTP/Files first; applies on the next restart.

Start the mission cycle automatically at server boot (-autoInit), so the persistent mission runs without waiting for an admin to log in. Needs a mission in server.cfg's class Missions; persistent = 1 is seeded by default. Applies on the next restart.

Paid add-on managed from the Headless Clients card on the server's Settings page (billed per client per month). Offloads AI for HC-aware missions (Antistasi, Liberation). Runs inside your server's resources with the same mods; applies on restart.
